Taking Stock of our Buildings 
The Climate Action Office has completed a new 
register of the Council’s buildings to help us plan 
how best to reduce their energy consumption and 
emissions. All public bodies are now required to 
develop a “Building Stock Register”. This will 
inform how to decarbonise building portfolio (i.e. 
move away from fossil fuels) through a combination 
of new buildings construction, retrofit of existing 
buildings, and the management of leased 
properties.

4 
 
The Register will also help us to prepare for the EU Energy Performance of Buildings Directive (EPBD), 
soon to be implemented. The EPBD requires all public sector bodies to implement Minimum Energy 
Performance Standards and also achieve a zero-emission building stock by 2050.  
 
The Register includes information on floor area, 
heating type, BER rating, details of retrofits etc. 
From 2024 we are obliged to report on this 
annually to the Sustainable Energy Authority of 
Ireland (SEAI).  There are currently 61 buildings 
on the Council’s Building Register, and the top five 
energy using buildings are the Watershed, County 
Hall, the Machinery Yard, Kilkenny Fire Station 
and the Watergate Theatre.  
 
 
 
Kilkenny County Council, in partnership with the other Local Authorities in the South East, are 
collaborating on the establishment of a Regional Energy Unit. Through this Unit Kilkenny County Council 
will apply for funding to the SEAI’s Pathfinder Programme to support us to decarbonise our building stock.

Green Schools 
The Environmental Awareness Officer (EAO) has assessed 17 schools within the County for their respective

The EAO is continuing to assist schools around the County to renew their membership as part of the Green

and Global Citizenship.  
 
Green schools is an international environmental education programme, offering a well-defined, controllable 
way for schools to take environmental issues into the curriculum and apply them to the day-to-day running 
of the school. Green schools is a holistic, long-term programme and has a two-year cycle in relation to 
preparation, assessment and attainment of a particular flag.

National Spring Clean 
National Spring Clean is Ireland’s most popular, well recognized and successful anti-litter initiative. Taking 
place during the whole month of April and now in its 25th year, the campaign encourages every sector of 
society to actively participate and take responsibility for litter by actually conducting clean ups in their own 
local environment. National Spring Clean traditionally takes place throughout the month of April.  
 
National Spring Clean has been operated by An Taisce since 1999 in partnership with the Department of 
Environment, Heritage & Local Government and Local Authorities. 
 
All community and voluntary groups are being encouraged to participate and register with An Taisce via 
About National Spring Clean - National Spring Clean. Groups can request additional supplies from the 
EAO via the Environmental Section.

In conjunction with the Enforcement Team in Environment, the EAO is coordinating a targeted campaign 
throughout the City and County on air quality and the continued use of smoky coals. The campaign seeks 
to raise awareness amongst the wider public, stakeholders, businesses and schools about the health and 
environmental impacts of poor air quality and the ways individuals can help reduce pollution. This will be 
a 4-6 week campaign commencing the week of the 15th of April 2024.

Anti-Litter and Anti-Graffiti Grant 2024 
Kilkenny County Council is offering community groups an opportunity this year to promote anti- litter and 
anti-graffiti awareness in their local community.  The grant is to mobilize community groups to care for 
their local environment by decreasing the impact of litter by its removal and to promote a social message 
locally to encourage everyone to put litter in its rightful place – in a bin. 
 
As funding comes directly from the Department of Communications, Climate Action & Environment there 
are funding restrictions which must be adhered to. 
 
This grant cannot cover:  
 
▪ 
the purchase of structural items such as street furniture 
▪ 
the purchase of litter bins 
▪ 
the purchase of dog bag dispensers  
▪ 
the purchase of signage 
▪ 
the purchase or rental of CCTV cameras  
 
The grant can cover expenses such as: 
 
▪ 
The purchase of bags for dog bag dispensers if dispensers are already installed at are under the care of 
the group. 
▪ 
The expense of litter disposal resulting from litter picks and the expense of disposal of rubbish from 
public street bins which are under the guardianship of the community group. 
▪ 
Awareness events highlighting the issue of litter and dog fouling in your local community. 
 
The application process will open on Monday 8th of April and applications can be accessed via our website: 
Environment - Kilkenny County Council (kilkennycoco.ie) or by contacting Deirdre.trait@kilkennycoco.ie  
 
Deadline for applications is the 24th of May, 2024.

regulations and has several active cases before the courts.

City.  Environment staff are continuing to work very closely with our service providers to ensure the 
collection service is in keeping with demand, especially around long weekends and holiday periods.

Callan Heritage Trail

panels. This project was conceived locally and the information provided by the Callan Heritage Society was 
really appreciated as it added so much richness to the story of Callan told through this new trail.
